Ana (Product): quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A about pricing/packaging — a customer asked two things and i want to capture here so we can turn into a doc/FAQ: 1) how do rate limits interact with Dedicated reserved capacity vs Hosted burst credits? 2) when do credits actually get consumed during retries/backoffs?

Leo (CEO): short answer: rate limiting (rps/concurrency) is enforced at the control plane/runtime level; billing (credits/tokens) is orthogonal. Hosted customers get a burst buffer on top of quotas; Dedicated customers have reserved throughput + optional burst lanes depending on contract. Credits are consumed when tokens are generated (not when request is enqueued).

Sandeep (Eng): to add some detail — enforcement model is layered: per-API-key TokenBucket for request ingress, per-model token accounting at emission time, and a cluster-level admission controller for Dedicated pools. Example policy snippet we use internally: 

```yaml
project_rate_limit:
  requests_per_minute: 6000
  burst_size: 200
model_emission_budget: 
  tokens_per_minute: 1_000_000
  billing_point: "on_emit"
```

Jess (Engineering): hosted behavior = short burst window (~5min) where extra RPS is served from a temporary burst bucket (consumed credits). After burst bucket drains, requests are either queued briefly or 429 depending on route SLOs. For Dedicated, if reserved GPUs are idle we let short bursts use reserved capacity (no extra credits) up to configured burst factor; beyond that we apply throttling or route to lower-cost fallbacks.

Mike (Finance): do overage charges auto-bill or do we require a human review for enterprise accounts? want to be clear for customer conversations.

Leo (CEO): Hosted = auto-consume prepay credits or invoice per-plan (depends on billing setup). Enterprise Dedicated = usually monthly committed spend; overages bill at negotiated rate but we surface alerts and require account approval for large overages by default.

Lisa (Support): can we get a short FAQ paragraph i can paste into support replies? customers keep asking about 429 vs tokens being charged.

Ana (Product): suggested blurb for support: "If you hit your plan's request rate we may temporarily return a 429. Tokens are only charged when the model emits tokens. For hosted customers we provide a short burst buffer that may consume credits; for Dedicated customers small bursts are often covered by reserved capacity — overage billing rules depend on your contract. If you're unsure, ping support with your org id and we'll check your burst & credit status."

Jess (Engineering): one operational gotcha — retries can cause extra token consumption if the retry reaches the model and the model emits before the client cancels. recommend clients use idempotency keys for non-streaming calls or use early-cancel on duplicate responses.

Sandeep (Eng): filing a small docs PR to capture exact numbers (burst window, default RPS, when 429 vs queue) and an internal runbook for SEs. I'll link the PR here when ready.

Ana (Product): action items: 1) @Sandeep create docs PR + /faq entry, 2) @Jess add note in runtime about "billing_point: on_emit" comment, 3) @Mike confirm enterprise overage workflow and default alerts, 4) @Lisa draft support snippet in Zendesk. I'll follow up and tag ops for final sign-off. :thumbsup:

DocsBot: docs PR created -> https://git.redwood.internal/docs/pull/4021 (contains proposed FAQ + config examples).

Ana (Product): awesome, thanks everyone — leaving this thread open for any nuance we missed. if you hit anything customer-facing pls paste into this thread before we publish.
